fields.description:
## Problem

Every CI job makes an avoidable network call to `raw.githubusercontent.com` before it can start, and when that call fails the job fails with `##[error]fetch failed` — a failure with no relationship to the change under test.

Observed 2026-08-28 on the `pip-audit` job of run 33214025855, which died after 21 seconds. The three consecutive log lines name the whole causal chain:

```
Could not determine uv version from uv.toml or pyproject.toml. Falling back ...
Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh ...
##[error]fetch failed
```

## Root cause

The `astral-sh/setup-uv` action is correctly SHA-pinned at every call site (`ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d  # v10.0.0`) — but **uv itself is not pinned**. There is no `version:` input at any call site, no `[tool.uv] required-version` in `pyproject.toml`, and no `uv.toml`.

Confirmed by reading the pinned action's own source at SHA `ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d`:

- `src/version/version-request-resolver.ts` — `WorkspaceVersionResolver.resolve` scans `getWorkspaceCandidates()`, which is exactly `<working-directory>/uv.toml` then `<working-directory>/pyproject.toml`. When neither yields a specifier it logs the observed line `"Could not determine uv version from uv.toml or pyproject.toml. Falling back to latest."` and returns `undefined`, so `LatestVersionResolver` supplies the specifier `"latest"`.
- `src/version/resolve.ts` — `LatestVersionResolver.resolve` calls `getLatestVersion(manifestUrl)`, which is the manifest fetch. By contrast `ExactVersionResolver.resolve` returns the normalized version immediately, **before** any resolver that touches the network is consulted (`CONCRETE_VERSION_RESOLVERS` orders exact first).
- `src/version/file-parser.ts` — the `pyproject.toml` parser reads `pyproject.tool?.uv?.["required-version"]` first, falling back to a `uv` dependency specifier.
- `src/version/specifier.ts` — `normalizeVersionSpecifier` strips a leading `==`, then `parseVersionSpecifier` classifies the result via `tc.isExplicitVersion`. So `required-version = "==0.12.7"` normalizes to `0.12.7`, classifies as `kind: "exact"`, and resolves with **no** network call. A range (`>=0.12.7`) classifies as `kind: "range"` and still fetches the manifest, so only an exact `==` pin removes the fetch.

The repository currently has **25** `setup-uv` call sites (the ticket's original "at least 8" undercounted; verified with `grep -rn "setup-uv@" .github/workflows/`), across `_build-and-test.yml`, `_eval-discipline.yml`, `_mutation.yml`, `dependency-advisory-canary.yml`, `external-integration.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `jira-dc-capability-map.yml`, `jira-dc-richtext-probe.yml`, `prompt-eval.yml`, `release.yml`, `structured-output-baseline.yml`, and `test.yml`. **No** call site sets `working-directory`, so every one of them resolves against the repository root, and every one is preceded in its job by a checkout step (24 by `actions/checkout`, and `gerrit-verify.yaml:178` by `lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action`). A single root-level pin therefore reaches all 25 without touching any call site.

`release.yml` is on the list, so an unpinned uv is also a supply-chain surface on the publishing path: the resolved version can change between runs without any change to the repository. This contradicts practice the project already applies elsewhere — `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` pins `acli` by version AND sha256 with the explicit instruction "Never run `latest` in CI."

## Approach

Add `[tool.uv] required-version = "==0.12.7"` to the root `pyproject.toml`, and add a guard that keeps that the single source of truth.

**Why `pyproject.toml` and not a new `.github/uv-version.txt`.** `setup-uv`'s zero-configuration workspace scan reads exactly two paths — `uv.toml` and `pyproject.toml` (`getWorkspaceCandidates`, cited above). Any other file, including a `.github/uv-version.txt` sibling of the existing `.github/python-version.txt`, would need a `version-file:` input added at all 25 call sites — which is the duplication the ticket's third acceptance criterion exists to prevent. `pyproject.toml` is the one file that is already committed, already read by the action with no inputs, and already read by uv itself. `uv.toml` would work for the action too, but is rejected: uv treats a `uv.toml` as a *replacement* for `[tool.uv]` in `pyproject.toml`, so creating one would silently orphan any future `[tool.uv]` setting added to `pyproject.toml`.

**Why `==0.12.7`.** That is what CI resolves to today, so the pin is a no-op for CI behavior rather than a silent upgrade or downgrade. Evidence from a real run — run 33225196631, job `build-and-test / lint + type-check`, 2026-08-29T01:08:42–43Z:

```
Could not determine uv version from uv.toml or pyproject.toml. Falling back to latest.
Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/main/v1/uv.ndjson ...
Downloading uv from "https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.12.7/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" ...
Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7
```

The same `0.12.7` appears in every other job of that run (`sweep (py3.14)`, `sweep (py3.15)`, `sweep (py3.14t)`, `sweep (macos, full suite)`), so it is the value in force across the matrix, not one job's accident.

**Accepted consequence: uv enforces the pin locally too.** `[tool.uv] required-version` is read by uv itself, not only by `setup-uv`. A contributor whose `uv` differs gets a hard error naming the fix — verified locally against uv 0.7.18 with a scratch `pyproject.toml` carrying `required-version = "==0.12.7"`:

```
error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.7.18`.
Update `uv` by running `uv self update 0.12.7`.
```

This is treated as a benefit rather than a cost: local uv 0.7.18 against CI's 0.12.7 is exactly the silent local/CI divergence that `make install`'s `uv sync --locked` is meant to prevent, and the pin converts it into a loud, self-describing, one-command fix. `docs/local-dev-env.md` gains a short note so a contributor meeting the error knows it is expected. This is the only behavior change outside CI, and it is stated here rather than discovered later.

**The guard.** A single-sourced pin has one realistic regression path: a later change adds a `version:` (or `version-file:`) input at one call site, which `ExplicitInputVersionResolver` honours **ahead of** the workspace scan, silently diverging that job from the project pin. `scripts/check_uv_pin.py` closes that path with three assertions — (1) `pyproject.toml` declares `[tool.uv] required-version` and its value is an exact `==X.Y.Z` specifier, not a range; (2) no `setup-uv` step in `.github/workflows/**` carries a `version:` or `version-file:` input; (3) no `uv.toml` exists at the repository root. It is wired into `make lint` alongside the existing `check_shellcheck.py` / `check_templatefile_escapes.py` gates, so it runs offline with no CI provider required (portability) and CI inherits it through the same `make lint` step.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — add the `[tool.uv]` section with `required-version = "==0.12.7"` and a comment stating why the `==` form is load-bearing.
- `scripts/check_uv_pin.py` — new guard implementing the three assertions above.
- `Makefile` — invoke the guard from the `lint` target.
- `tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` — new; proves the guard passes on the real tree and fails on each skew.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — note the pin and the `uv self update` remedy.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — one entry.

No `.github/workflows/**` file is modified: the whole point of the chosen mechanism is that all 25 call sites are fixed without editing any of them. The `setup-uv` action SHA pins are left exactly as they are.

## Testing

**Guard unit tests** (`tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py`), each building a temporary tree and invoking the checker against it, so the failure modes are proven rather than asserted:

- Happy path: the checker returns exit 0 against this repository's real root.
- Skew — a workflow file whose `setup-uv` step carries `version: "0.11.0"` makes the checker exit non-zero and name that file. This is the "prove the check FAILS when one site is deliberately skewed" requirement; without it the guard is a check that can only pass.
- Skew — `required-version = ">=0.12.7"` (a range, which per `parseVersionSpecifier` still triggers the manifest fetch) makes the checker exit non-zero.
- Skew — `[tool.uv] required-version` absent entirely makes the checker exit non-zero.
- Skew — a root `uv.toml` present makes the checker exit non-zero.

**Real-CI-log verification, with a liveness anchor.** After the change is pushed for review, the Gerrit Verified run over this change is inspected with `gh run view <id> --log`. A grep returning zero matches proves nothing on its own — an empty log, a skipped step, or a job that never reached setup all produce zero matches — so the assertion is ordered:

1. **Liveness anchor first**: the log MUST contain `Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7`. That line is emitted by the action only after it has actually installed uv, so its presence proves the setup step ran, and its value simultaneously proves the installed version equals the pin. (This is a stronger claim than "the fallback message disappeared", and is asserted separately from it.)
2. **Only then** assert absence: the log MUST NOT contain `Could not determine uv version`, and MUST NOT contain `raw.githubusercontent.com`.
3. A positive line proving the new source was read is also expected — the action logs `Found version for uv in <path>: 0.12.7` (`file-parser.ts` `getParsedVersionFile`) — and is recorded as corroboration.

The verification is run against the change's own CI, and both the anchor and the absences are recorded verbatim in a ticket comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pyproject.toml` contains `[tool.uv]` with `required-version = "==0.12.7"`; checked by `grep -A2 '^\[tool\.uv\]' pyproject.toml`.
- [ ] No `.github/workflows/**` file gains a `version:` or `version-file:` input on a `setup-uv` step; checked by `git diff --stat origin/main -- .github/workflows` reporting no changed files.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_uv_pin.py` exits 0 on the tree; and exits non-zero on each of the four skews, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` passing.
- [ ] `make lint` invokes `scripts/check_uv_pin.py`; checked by `make lint` succeeding and `grep -n check_uv_pin Makefile` matching inside the `lint` target.
- [ ] A real CI log for this change contains `Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7` (liveness anchor + version match) AND contains neither `Could not determine uv version` nor `raw.githubusercontent.com`; the three grep results are pasted into a ticket comment.
- [ ] Upgrading uv is a one-line change: the version appears exactly once in a non-test, non-doc source file; checked by `grep -rn '0\.12\.7' pyproject.toml Makefile scripts/check_uv_pin.py` matching only the `pyproject.toml` line.
